# prism-chronology Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Chronology: Decides how two time intervals relate, as one of Allen's thirteen interval relations, so the Prism can order events and find schedule conflicts exactly.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never malformed when astart is below aend and bstart is below bend

The app SHALL NOT answer `malformed` when astart is below aend and bstart is below bend, because two real intervals must always get a relation.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 120 180` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `malformed`
- **AND** the app answers `before`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never before when aend is at least bstart

The app SHALL NOT answer `before` when aend is at least bstart, because an event that runs into another must never be ordered before it.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 60 120` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `before`
- **AND** the app answers `meets`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never after when bend is at least astart

The app SHALL NOT answer `after` when bend is at least astart, because an event another runs into must never be ordered after it.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 120 180` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `after`
- **AND** the app answers `before`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never equals when astart differs from bstart

The app SHALL NOT answer `equals` when astart differs from bstart, because different starts must never be called the same time.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 120 180` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `equals`
- **AND** the app answers `before`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never equals when aend differs from bend

The app SHALL NOT answer `equals` when aend differs from bend, because different ends must never be called the same time.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 120 180` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `equals`
- **AND** the app answers `before`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never meets when aend differs from bstart

The app SHALL NOT answer `meets` when aend differs from bstart, because meets must mean back to back exactly.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 120 180` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `meets`
- **AND** the app answers `before`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never during when astart is at most bstart

The app SHALL NOT answer `during` when astart is at most bstart, because during must mean strictly inside.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-007, theorem `inv007Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-007 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 120 180` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `during`
- **AND** the app answers `before`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never overlaps when aend is below bstart

The app SHALL NOT answer `overlaps` when aend is below bstart, because separate events must never be reported as a conflict.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-008, theorem `inv008Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-008 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 120 180` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `overlaps`
- **AND** the app answers `before`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-001 malformed when aend is at most astart

The app SHALL answer `malformed` when aend is at most astart, because A must end after it starts.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `malformed`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Otherwise overlappedby

The app SHALL answer `overlappedby` when no rule matches, because Allen: overlapped by, the only relation left.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `90 150 60 120` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `overlappedby`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `0 60 120 180` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `before`, decided by REQ-003, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 4 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `before`, `meets`, `overlaps`, `starts`, `during`, `finishes`, `equals`, `after`, `metby`, `overlappedby`, `startedby`, `contains`, `finishedby`, `malformed`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `astart` | whole number from 0 up to 10080 | when interval A starts, in minutes since the start of the week |
| `aend` | whole number from 0 up to 10080 | when interval A ends, in minutes since the start of the week |
| `bstart` | whole number from 0 up to 10080 | when interval B starts, in minutes since the start of the week |
| `bend` | whole number from 0 up to 10080 | when interval B ends, in minutes since the start of the week |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `before` | A ends before B starts |
| `meets` | A ends exactly when B starts |
| `overlaps` | A starts first and ends inside B |
| `starts` | both start together and A ends first |
| `during` | A lies strictly inside B |
| `finishes` | both end together and A starts later |
| `equals` | same start and same end |
| `after` | A starts after B ends |
| `metby` | A starts exactly when B ends |
| `overlappedby` | B starts first and ends inside A |
| `startedby` | both start together and B ends first |
| `contains` | B lies strictly inside A |
| `finishedby` | both end together and B starts later |
| `malformed` | an interval does not end after it starts |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 4 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Out of scope

- Times are whole minutes within one week; longer spans need a larger unit.
- Intervals include their start and exclude their end, so back-to-back events meet and do not overlap.
- Time zones are resolved before the request; both intervals use the same clock.

## Examples

- `0 60 120 180` gives `before`
- `0 60 60 120` gives `meets`
- `0 90 60 120` gives `overlaps`
- `60 90 60 120` gives `starts`
- `70 90 60 120` gives `during`
- `90 120 60 120` gives `finishes`
- `60 120 60 120` gives `equals`
- `200 260 60 120` gives `after`
- `120 180 60 120` gives `metby`
- `90 150 60 120` gives `overlappedby`
- `60 150 60 120` gives `startedby`
- `0 200 60 120` gives `contains`
- `0 120 60 120` gives `finishedby`
- `60 60 0 30` gives `malformed`
- `0 30 90 80` gives `malformed`
- `540 600 570 630` gives `overlaps`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
